papers.title: Synergistic effects of surface chemistry and topologic structure from modified microarc oxidation coatings on Ti implants for improving osseointegration.
papers.abstract: Microarc oxidation (MAO) coating containing Ca, P, Si, and Na elements on a titanium (Ti) implant has been steam-hydrothermally treated and further mediated by post-heat treatment to overcome the compromised bone-implant integration. The bone regeneration, bone-implant contact, and biomechanical push-out force of the modified Ti implants are discussed thoroughly in this work. The best in vivo performances for the steam-hydrothermally treated one is attributed to the synergistic effects of surface chemistry and topologic structure. Through post-heat treatment, we can decouple the effects of surface chemistry and the nanoscale topologic structure easily. Attributed to the excellent in vivo performance of the surface-modified Ti implant, the steam-hydrothermal treatment could be a promising strategy to improve the osseointegration of the MAO coating covered Ti implant.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the synergistic effects of surface chemistry and topological structure on improving osseointegration of titanium implants.
summary_en.method: Microarc oxidation coatings were modified via steam-hydrothermal treatment and post-heat treatment.
summary_en.result: Steam-hydrothermal treatment significantly enhanced bone regeneration, bone-implant contact, and push-out force.
summary_en.validation: In vivo animal experiments were conducted to evaluate osseointegration.
